title: Orchestrate approval threads and contingency lanes for PRD review & sign-off
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Goal: Define a clear, traceable acceptance and escalation path for the new PRD (model onboarding + structured output controls) so Engineering, Design, and Legal can complete reviews and sign-offs without blocking the Q2 rollout. This ticket codifies meeting cadence, decision owners, acceptance matrix, contingency lanes (fallthrough approvals, canary rollback triggers), and artifact links needed for sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Formal acceptance matrix published that maps each acceptance criterion to a named owner from Eng/Design/Legal by 2026-03-18
All open legal questions from initial review resolved or assigned with expected resolution dates
Design has provided staged UX flows (canary/rollback states) and linked components to the Console backlog
Engineering has confirmed API compatibility and a migration path, including model-version pinning and fallback behavior
A rollout contingency plan with explicit rollback triggers and communication owners is documented and reviewed
Telemetry checks and observability queries required for acceptance are defined and their dashboards referenced
comments: 2026-03-11 Kickoff: Eng/Design/Legal present. Agreed scope: initial PRD covers model onboarding + structured output gating for Private deployments. Action: PM to draft acceptance matrix.
2026-03-12 Design feedback: request for two staged UIs for rollouts (canary toggle + manual rollback). Designer assigned: DES-314 to deliver mocks by 2026-03-17.
2026-03-12 Engineering notes: kernel selection and quantization fallback behavior needs explicit API flags. ENG-58412 to prototype a safety fallback within two sprints.
2026-03-12 Legal checklist: data residency and audit log retention items flagged. Legal needs dataflow diagram and list of PII fields. Action: PM to collect from Eng by 2026-03-15.

2026-03-13 Tradeoff discussion: aggressive caching reduces cost but increases risk of stale structured outputs. Decision: include cache TTL as part of acceptance criteria and require a canary with TTL=0 for first 48h post-rollout.

2026-03-13 Risk note: dependency on ENG-59003 (runtime autoscale guard) — if autoscale cannot honor per-tenant isolation, we must delay private rollout. Contingency lane: degrade to hosted-only for affected customers.
2026-03-13 PM action: publish acceptance matrix draft and invite owners to review (deadline 2026-03-18). If any owner does not respond, escalate to their manager and schedule a decision sync.
Links added: PRD draft, design mocks, and prototype checklist included in links field below. Will attach GH PR references when available.
open_questions: Can Legal sign off on telemetry payloads that contain token-level spans? (Legal asked for redaction guidance)
What is the minimum observability signal set required to declare a canary healthy? (Eng to propose SLO gates)
Does Design require additional A11y review for the canary UI path?
If an owner misses the acceptance deadline, what is the formal escalation cadence?
action_items: PM (Jordan) to publish acceptance matrix draft by 2026-03-15
Design (DES-314) to deliver mocks and staged interaction notes by 2026-03-17
Engineering (ENG-58412) to provide a prototype of fallback behavior and an initial compatibility checklist by 2026-03-24
Legal to supply an approvals checklist and dataflow requirements by 2026-03-18
SRE/Console to prepare canary dashboard and alert hooks referenced in the release runbook by 2026-03-25
